# How much sensing is enough? Collective inference for insect-neuron sensor networks

*One-page technical abstract, proofread final (2026-09-10). Every number below is recomputed from `netsim/out/summary.csv` by `python -m netsim.verify_abstract`; the CSV is regenerated by `bash netsim/reproduce.sh`.*

**Problem.** Continuous electrophysiological telemetry from insect neurons is a
candidate low-cost sensor for chemical, pharmacological and radiological hazards
in industrial settings. The single-sensor question, *how early does one neuron
flag a perturbation*, has been asked before; the deployment question has not:
given real single-unit statistics, how many sensors, in which layout, and with
which collective decision rule are needed to raise an alarm before the first
loss of function at the source, at a fixed false-alarm rate, and how well can
the network locate that source?

**Approach and methodology.** Single-unit inter-spike-interval statistics were
fitted by maximum likelihood (gamma renewal with absolute refractory period) to
openly licensed cockroach (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14281, n = 12 units) and locust
(10.5281/zenodo.14607, n = 4) antennal-lobe recordings; these fits are the only
empirical input. A neurotoxic front is simulated as a radial wave (1.5 domain
units/s) behind which firing rate decays with time constant 8 s; the endpoint is
the first collapse at the source (rate < 5 % of baseline for 2 s), which by
construction does not depend on sensor placement. Between 4 and 100 sensors are
placed on a jittered grid, uniformly at random, or in three clusters, and report 1 s spike
counts with log-normal measurement noise (sd 0, 0.15, 0.30). Three single-node
statistics (z-score, one-sided CUSUM, Bayesian online changepoint posterior of a
depressed regime) are combined by three network rules (max over sensors; mean
over 4 nearest neighbours then max; count above a per-detector level). Each
pipeline's threshold is set on 40 null runs to a per-run false-alarm
probability of 0.05; realised false-alarm rate comes from 20 held-out null
runs, and 20 perturbed runs per cell give detection probability, lead time and
localisation error (54 cells × 9 pipelines).

**Key findings.** (1) Spatial pooling dominates: averaged over all cells,
CUSUM with k-NN pooling detects before collapse in 75 % of runs with a mean lead
of 6.8 s and a localisation error of 6.8 % of the domain diagonal, against 63 %
and 5.4 s for the same statistic with the max rule, at the same realised
false-alarm rate (0.06–0.08). (2) Layout matters as much as count (CUSUM + pooling,
noise 0.15): on a grid, 16 sensors reach 95 % detection with ~7 s lead, random
placement needs 36 for the same, and clustered placement reaches 80 % only at 64
sensors and never reaches 100 % in the range tested. (3) Lead time saturates:
even 100 grid sensors give 7–13 s (pooled rules, all noise levels) against a
theoretical maximum of 26 s, so beyond ~36 sensors the marginal sensor buys
localisation, not time. (4) The max
rule does not scale for bounded statistics: BOCPD+max falls from 80 % detection
at 9 sensors to 10 % at 100, because the null maximum over many sensors pushes
the calibrated threshold toward the statistic's ceiling; pooled BOCPD stays at
100 %. (5) With 16 grid sensors the best pipeline keeps ≥ 95 % detection at every
noise level tested, up to sd 0.30.

**Limitations and future work.** Ground truth is simulated: this answers a
network-design question, not a biological one, and the isotropic front with
exponential decay stands in for real toxicodynamics. Rate is the only feature
(1 s bins, 3-bin sustain rule); ISI-shape features and the learned detector in
`ml/` are unused. Next: validate the single-node model on recordings with a
documented pharmacological intervention, add ISI-shape features to the network
statistic, and close the loop with the platform's hardware-in-the-loop nodes.

**Reproducibility.** `bash netsim/reproduce.sh` runs the 21 unit tests and the
full sweep (~4 min) and writes `netsim/out/RESULTS.md`, the CSVs and the
figures; `python -m netsim.verify_abstract` re-derives every number above from
`summary.csv`. The simulator is also an MCP server for AI research agents.
